questions.question: How should I handle the JARs being on the public mirror?

options.label: Re-private + fix + republish (Recommended)
options.description: Immediately set dstrader-docker-public to private via API. File a small PR on daily-driver introducing `sync-exclude.txt` mechanism (per SOP §6 "Exclusion mechanism") listing the JARs. After merge, re-run Step 6b with exclusion, set public again. Matches `public-track-rollback-acceptable` playbook. Minimizes ongoing exposure.

options.label: Force-push re-sync without JARs (stay public)
options.description: Leave dstrader-docker-public public. File the same daily-driver `sync-exclude.txt` PR. Immediately force-push a new single-commit snapshot without the JARs (6b allows this). JARs stay technically retrievable from GitHub's server-side dangling refs for some hours until GC, but cloners of the new state won't see them. Faster, less ceremony, slightly leakier.

options.label: Accept — dstrader Java is going public anyway
options.description: Per three-tier strategy, `jdtogni78/dstrader` (Java source) is also slated for public sync. The JARs being public now is just earlier. Skip remediation; let dstrader Java go public on its own timeline. Note this decision on #16.

options.label: Re-private only, plan remediation later
options.description: Set dstrader-docker-public to private right now to stop the bleed. Don't rush the daily-driver PR or re-sync. Owner decides timeline. Conservative; pauses progress.
